correctness.rationale: Writing the Gram operator as I+P_T−Q_B, principal bases for the two rank-two subspaces split the difference into two blocks with trace zero and determinant −(1−σ²), where σ is the corresponding cross-Gram singular value. Orthogonal pairs give ±1, common directions give two zeros per coincident angle when counted with the complementary dimensions, and the balance is n−4 zeros; this includes the double 1 in the n=4 singular case. The two cross-Gram squared singular values are 2(1±|cos(πab/n)|)/n by the squared row lengths and the inner-product modulus. The smallest and largest frame eigenvalues sum to 2; singularity is ab≡0. The optimum selects the available residues closest to n/2, all attainable using a=1. For nonzero a of gcd d, ab=k has d solutions if d|k and none otherwise; excluding b=0 removes one only for k=0, and there are φ(n/d) choices of a. Multiplying by n² for origins and dividing by four for the two orderings of each unordered pair gives the two counts. Taylor expansion gives the stated second-order coefficients, and the eigenvalue ratio under a square root is the spectral condition number. Private replay: python3 /workspace/branches/check_fourier_spectrum.py (NumPy). It checked all eigenvalues for 501 difference pairs and independently enumerated unordered counts for n=4..12. The frozen checker builds full matrices but asserts only the two extreme eigenvalues and their sum; it was inspected, not executed. The finite checks, including the new checks of the entire multiset, supplement the proof.

evidence: For a fixed B with d=gcd(n,b), the prior m=n/d classes contain d sites each. Coincident phases give exactly m·binomial(d,2)=n(d−1)/2 singular time pairs. This is the earlier r=2 same-phase worst count when d≥2; it is zero when d=1.

In even n, an exactly antipodal phase pair is possible iff m is even, equivalently d|n/2; exactly (m/2)d² time pairs attain it for this B. In odd n, minimizing the known cosine profile across B requires m=n (the smallest value is sin(π/(2m))), and there are n unordered closest-to-antipodal time pairs per such B. There are nφ(n/d)/2 frequency pairs of each gcd d. These counts give exactly both frozen optimal formulas and the singular formula.
